original_question: For G2 Costas arrays constructed over finite fields of characteristic 2, determine the four parity populations ee, eo, oe, and oo, namely the numbers of dots whose coordinates are respectively even-even, even-odd, odd-even, and odd-odd.
target_in_paper: Section 7.1, Problem 17: Determine the parity populations of G2 arrays constructed in fields of characteristic 2.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It identifies the correct family of Costas arrays (G2), the correct ambient setting (finite fields of characteristic 2), and the correct four parity populations ee, eo, oe, and oo with the intended meanings as counts of dots in even-even, even-odd, odd-even, and odd-odd positions.
missing_details: It should define precisely what a G2 array is in the sense of the paper: a Golomb G2 Costas array coming from Theorem 3.
It should specify the field as F(q) with q = 2^m, and quantify over all such characteristic-2 fields for which the G2 construction applies.
It should specify the construction data: primitive roots alpha and beta of F(2^m), and the G2 permutation f:[q-2] -> [q-2] defined by alpha^{f(i)} + beta^i = 1.
It should state the array order q-2 and the array/permutation correspondence, namely that the dots of the associated Costas array are at positions (f(i), i).
It should make explicit that parity refers to the ordinary integer parity of the row and column indices in [q-2] x [q-2], not to any field-theoretic notion.

It should acknowledge the paper's nearby observation that, in characteristic 2, these populations may depend on the chosen primitive roots alpha and beta, so the task is to determine that dependence or characterize all possible values across the G2 family.
It should clarify that the goal is exact determination of the parity populations for the whole characteristic-2 G2 family, not just reporting numerical data.
refined_question: For each finite field F(2^m) with q = 2^m > 2, and for each pair of primitive roots alpha, beta in F(q), let f:[q-2] -> [q-2] be the Golomb G2 Costas permutation defined by alpha^{f(i)} + beta^i = 1 for i in [q-2]. In the associated Costas array A_f, whose dots are at positions (f(i), i), determine the four parity populations ee, eo, oe, and oo, where ee, eo, oe, and oo denote respectively the numbers of dots with row-column parity even-even, even-odd, odd-even, and odd-odd. Equivalently, determine these populations exactly for all G2 arrays constructed over fields of characteristic 2, including any dependence on the choice of alpha and beta.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for each characteristic-2 G2 permutation f:[q-2] -> [q-2] defined by alpha^{f(i)} + beta^i = 1 over F(2^m), determine the cardinalities of the four sets {i in [q-2] : f(i) is even and i is even}, {i in [q-2] : f(i) is even and i is odd}, {i in [q-2] : f(i) is odd and i is even}, and {i in [q-2] : f(i) is odd and i is odd}.
justification: This draft matches the paper's Problem 17 almost verbatim, so the correct target is exactly Section 7.1's open problem on parity populations of G2 arrays in characteristic 2. The only substantial omissions are the paper's implicit definitions: Theorem 3 supplies the precise meaning of a G2 array via the equation alpha^{f(i)} + beta^i = 1 over F(p^m), specialized here to p = 2, and Definition 1 supplies the array/permutation correspondence needed to interpret the parity of dot coordinates. Section 7.1 also makes clear that, unlike the odd-characteristic case, the populations in characteristic 2 vary across the G2 family, so the refined question should allow dependence on the chosen primitive roots rather than presupposing a uniform formula.
